title: ROBERT ELLIS Band at FITZGERALDS w/ special guest Philip Bowen
description: FITZGERALDS NIGHTCLUB PRESENTS: Robert Ellis at FITZGERALDS Nightclub w/ special guest Philip Bowen $25 General Admission / Reserved Tables Available Recorded live to tape in just two days, Robert Ellis's exquisite new album, Yesterday's News, is as stripped-down as it gets, with the celebrated songwriter and producer's delicate, reedy tenor accompanied only by nylon string guitar, upright bass, and the occasional piece of handheld percussion. The arrangements are harmonically sophisticated here, drawing on the open tunings and intricate fingerpicking of English songwriters like Nick Drake or Richard Thompson, and Ellis's performances are similarly subtle and nuanced, tapping into the bittersweet longing of Chet Baker and the playful poignancy of Bill Evans and Jim Hall. While that might seem surprising coming off 2019's raucous Texas Piano Man, subverting expectations is nothing new for Ellis. Born and raised outside Houston, he gained early acclaim for his piercing introspection and absorbing narratives, but over the course of five solo albums, he flirted with everything from Paul Simon and John Prine to Elton John and Joni Mitchell in a series of sonic and visual transformations that ran the gamut from Redneck Steely Dan to Lone Star Liberace. NPR hailed his , "rdquo" -> musical daring and impeccable songcraft," while Rolling Stone praised his , "rdquo" -> sharp eye for storytelling," and the New York Times lauded his writing as an emotional , "rdquo" -> gut punch." Yesterday's News marks Ellis's debut LP for Niles City Records, an outgrowth of the famed Niles City Sound studio he and longtime collaborator Josh Block run in Fort Worth, TX. title: TERRAPIN FLYER: A Grateful Dead Tribute @ FITZGERALDS!
description: FITZGERALDS NIGHTCLUB PRESENTS: TERRAPIN FLYER: A Grateful Dead Tribute $25 General Admission // $30/seat Reserved Tables For more than 25 years, Terrapin Flyer has been a powerhouse of the national music scene, renowned for their faithful yet adventurous interpretations of Grateful Dead classics. Originally formed in 1999, the band has built a storied legacy through long-term collaborations with Dead legends like Melvin Seals, Vince Welnick, and Tom Constanten, earning them a spot in Rolling Stone's "Guide to the Grateful Dead." By blending tight musicianship with free-flowing improvisation and a deep reverence for jazz, blues, and bluegrass, the current lineup---featuring Josh Olken, Wavy Dave, Jon Reed, Michael Cole, and Doug Hagman---channels the authentic spirit of a true Dead show where every performance is a unique, soul-stirring experience. title: Hawktober at Lakeside Community Center
venue: Lakeside Community Center,9841 Vine St, Lakeside, CA 92040, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

title: Día de los Muertos Celebration
description: Join the San Diego Automotive Museum for our first-ever Día de los Muertos Celebration, honoring the rich traditions of this meaningful holiday with a day of family-friendly activities followed by an unforgettable evening of live music. Día de los Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a Mexican tradition that honors and remembers loved ones who have passed. At the heart of the celebration are remembrance, family, and community. As part of the museum’s celebration, guests will have the opportunity to experience traditional elements of Día de los Muertos while surrounded by some of the world’s most beautiful and historic vehicles.

description: The Art Glass Guild will be hosting their 2026 Fall Patio Show and Sale on October 10th and 11th. Visitors will see the patio full of juried artists exhibiting their creations as they stroll through Spanish Village Art Center in Balboa Park. Beautiful art glass exhibiting techniques such as: blown, fused, torch, stained, cast, and etched will be on display with the artist right there to explain or show how it is done. title: Pumpkin Chunkin’

address: 2001 Pan American Plaza, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Get ready for a day of engineering, coding, creativity, and flying pumpkins! Pumpkin Chunkin’ is returning to the San Diego Air & Space Museum on October 10, from 10 am to 1 pm bringing hands-on STEM challenges and plenty of Halloween fun for kids and families. This year, we’re excited to welcome a local high school robotics team, who will show visitors some of their amazing robot creations and demonstrate what goes into designing, building, and coding a competition robot. Young engineers can then try their own hand at solving Halloween-themed challenges throughout the museum. Activities will include: Build a Catapult: Design and construct a catapult, then see how far you can launch a candy pumpkin! Pumpkin Parachutes: Create a parachute designed to help a pumpkin make a safe landing. 3D Pen Spider Webs: Experiment with 3D pens to create creepy-crawly spider webs. Code a Mouse: Program a robotic mouse to navigate its way through a maze. Create a Monster: Use if-then statements to design a monster that reacts to different situations. And, of course, the highlight of Pumpkin Chunkin’ is the moment everyone waits for the PUMPKIN DROP! Watch as pumpkins take flight in a spectacular finale that combines a little Halloween fun with a lot of physics and engineering. There will be one small difference this year: the museum is currently covered in scaffolding as part of ongoing work on the building. So a new and exciting pumpkin platform will be used. Halloween Fun for Everyone Pumpkin Chunkin’ is included with museum admission, and October is Kids Free Month at the San Diego Air & Space Museum! During October, up to two children per one paid adult admission can visit the museum for free. Youth groups are welcome, too! Groups of 10–25 youth and their chaperones can attend for free with advance registration. To preregister your group, email education@sdasm.org . Costumes are welcome! Come dressed as your favorite astronaut, scientist, robot, monster, or anything else you can imagine. Join us for Pumpkin Chunkin’ and discover that some of the best Halloween fun comes with a little engineering mixed in!

description: Taking turns at an onstage piano, the dual tribute artists of the Billy Joel/Elton John Face 2 Face? Tribute Show conjure the beloved songsters in both sound and image. Backed by his band The Stranger, Levittown, NY native Mike Santoro?s fingers flash up and down the keys before he jumps up to grab the mic to belt out such high-energy Billy Joel classics as ?Uptown Girl? and ?Only the Good Die Young.? For the second half of the roughly three-hour show, Ronnie Smith dons the iconic sunglasses and bedazzled suits of Elton John as he charts his style from the ?70s to the present. Bittersweet anthems such as ?Rocket Man (I Think It?s Going to Be a Long, Long Time)? mix with more whimsical material such as ?Crocodile Rock? and the fictional rock-group narrative ?Bennie and the Jets.? During each engaging, interactive show, both acts aim to channel the spirit of their originals so well that audiences will forget they?re a tribute!

description: Longevity in music comes through pushing yourself and expanding the possibilities of your sound. This has never been more true for Copeland. The band, which originally formed in Lakeland, Florida in 2001, has unveiled six albums, spanning from their 2003s debut Beneath Medicine Tree to 2016s Ixora. While they began as a rock band, Copelands music has explored multiple genres and pulled in various stylistic influences like electronic and symphonic. In the past the musicians have aptly melded these styles, creating a unique amalgam of sounds. This time they wanted to take each sound and style and push it to its logical extreme.

title: Armand Hammer with Quelle Chris and Open Mike Eagle
description: For nearly a decade as a duo, and longer still as solo artists, Armand Hammer have left a palpable mark on modern rap and hip-hop. At turns both sharp-witted and soul-crushing, their lyrics unspool threads of socio-political, historical, and philosophical import with a potent blend of incisive critique, gallows humor, and narrative élan. Mercy is the first Armand Hammer album since 2023's We Buy Diabetic Test Strips, a project that The Observer (UK) described as "an exceptional record that deserves your time and headphones" and The Line Of Best Fit deemed "their headiest and most impressive work thus far." On 2021's Haram, their first with The Alchemist, the duo "drag postcolonial wounds onto the examination table" (Pitchfork). Beats Per Minute called it "a tremendous success." Earlier this year, billy woods released GOLLIWOG, ", "rdquo" -> a densely poetic, totally masterful tour de force" (Rolling Stone) and "one of 2025's truly essential albums" (The FADER). Meanwhile, ELUCID's "enthralling" (MOJO) 2024 album REVELATOR was described by Pitchfork as "soul food for those who know a better world is possible if we're willing to fight for it." The New York Times, in naming REVELATOR one of their Best Albums Of 2024, called it "a dense, overdriven, fiercely abrasive album that cranks up the tradition of Public Enemy's Bomb Squad productions for 21st-century impact."

description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

description: Visit real astronomers from the San Diego Astronomy Association and look through their big, beautiful telescopes at Mother Nature's night light display. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. title: Art Glass Guild Show and Sale
address: 1770 Village Pl, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: The Art Glass Guild will be hosting their 2026 Fall Patio Show and Sale on October 10th and 11th. This show is the largest Art Glass show in Southern California and is focused on showcasing art created by local San Diego Glass Artists. Visitors will see the patio full of juried artists exhibiting their creations as they stroll through Spanish Village Art Center in Balboa Park. Beautiful art glass exhibiting techniques such as: blown, fused, torch, stained, cast, and etched will be on display with the artist right there to explain or show how it is done. There will be entertainment for all including, a demonstration featuring torch-work, as well as an area for children and adults alike to create their own unique mosaic art piece to take home. The Art Glass Guild is a non-profit art education center, focused on supporting local glass artists as well as other San Diego non-profits with art related programs benefiting the community. “This is a fun family outing to see an array of beautiful art glass, glass demonstrations and free mosaic make and take and also to support our local artists,” says Helen Munroe, Fused Glass Artist and member of The Art Glass Guild. The event is free to the public and pet friendly.

title: Interpol - North America Tour 2026 with DIIV
description: This Mirror Weighs a Ton, finds the band turning inward while continuing to move forward. Across the record, reflection, distortion and perception become a lens through which familiar shapes are refracted into something slightly alien, as if seen through a different kind of light. Synthesizers, strings, acoustic guitars and percussion are integrated into the fabric of the songs, expanding the palette while revealing colors already latent within it. Nothing feels imposed. Instead, the additions deepen the band?s language of restraint, atmosphere and tension. The result is an album that feels expansive, uncanny and alive with forward motion, not a reinvention but an evolution that allows Interpol to continue transforming without losing their identity.

description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts. title: An Evening With Steve Dawson with special guests Jason Adasiewicz, Jason Roebke, Diane Christiansen and Alton Smith
description: One of the lynchpins of Chicagos flourishing songwriter scene is Steve Dawson, a songwriter and vocalist who elevates everything he touches. - WBEZ Chicago An evocative, brilliant songwriter who imbues his songs and recordings with folk, country, and a smattering of soul he should, by all rights, be a household name. - Popmatters Steve Dawson will look back over 35 years of songs and music making, including songs from his first Chicago band, Stump The Host, through Dolly Varden, Funeral Bonsai Wedding and up to his more recent critically acclaimed solo albums, Ghosts, and At The Bottom of a Canyon in the Branches of a Tree. Over the course of 6 albums with Dolly Varden, 4 solo albums, and 2 albums with the jazz / folk combo, Funeral Bonsai Wedding, Dawson has delved into all corners of American music and dug deep into the mysteries and wonders of life, mortality, love and memory. Dawson will be joined by a few guest musicians for this evenings show. Originally from San Diego, California, he spent his teen years in Hailey, Idaho, where he learned guitar and started writing songs. After a few years at the Berklee School of Music in Boston, Dawson moved to Chicago and formed the band, Stump the Host, with his future wife, artist and singer, Diane Christiansen. Later he formed, recorded and toured with Dolly Varden and Funeral Bonsai Wedding. More recently he has created critically acclaimed solo albums for the Pravda record label. Dawson also teaches songwriting at the legendary Old Town School of Folk Music and co-wrote a book on songwriting and the creative process with Mark Caro called, Take It To The Bridge: Unlocking The Great Songs Inside You. In 2020 Dawson was awarded the Esteemed Artist Award from the City of Chicago.

title: BEAT: Belew/Vai/Levin/Bozzio Performing the Music of KING CRIMSON
description: Following more than 100 acclaimed performances across North and South America, Europe, and Japan, BEAT returns this fall for the last North American tour. Former King Crimson members Adrian Belew and Tony Levin are joined by guitar virtuoso Steve Vai and legendary drummer Terry Bozzio to perform the music of the three landmark 1980s King Crimson albums---Discipline, Beat, and Three of a Perfect Pair. Rather than attempting to recreate the original recordings, BEAT brings this extraordinary music to life with the spirit, precision, and adventurousness that made it so enduring. Whether you've lived with these albums for decades or are discovering them for the first time, this is the final opportunity to experience one of progressive music's most celebrated catalogs performed by four of the best musicians on the planet.

title: The Best of The Second City
The Burney Sisters
description: The Burney Sisters are a powerhouse sibling duo redefining indie-folk with their soulful harmonies, heartfelt lyrics, and magnetic stage presence. Originally from the Midwest, sisters Emma and Bella Burney create music that blends folk, indie, and Americana into a sound that feels both timeless and fresh. Drawing inspiration from iconic artists like Paul Simon and Lake Street Dive, as well as contemporary trailblazers like Lizzy McAlpine, Madison Cunningham, Phoebe Bridgers, and First Aid Kit The Burney Sisters bridge generations with a style that is uniquely their own. Emma's multi-instrumental talents---on piano, violin, guitar, and cello---pair seamlessly with Bella's commanding basslines, showcasing a maturity and versatility far beyond their years. Their music explores themes of love, resilience, and self-discovery with a raw honesty that resonates deeply with fans of all ages. For the past eight years, The Burney Sisters have traveled extensively, performing across the U.S., Canada, and the Caribbean. Their journey has not only shaped their sound but also fueled their passion for connecting through music.

title: White Denim w. Arc Iris
description: Ive always wanted to make work thats a reflection of my life experience, says singer-guitarist James Petralli, leader of venturous L.A.-based rockers White Denim. The just-below-the-surface significance to 13 as an album title is that I was born on the thirteenth of August. 13 in numerology can signify independence, creativity, and a solid foundation, but inversely is often considered to be unlucky and can signify chaos and misfortune. Like everyone, I can certainly see both sides in my life.13 also happens to be the thirteenth album of White Denims career. An incandescent, groove-heavy alchemy of rock, funk, dub, soul and down-dirty blues and plenty more besides its imbued with the same questing spirit thats been the bands trademark since first starting in Austin, Texas, some 20 years ago.Petrallis wide-ranging musical appetites have become more voracious over time. The sounds and textures of 13 are informed by everyone from Scritti Politti to The Gap Band, Terry Reid to King Tubby, Caetano Veloso to John Cale, Stevie Wonder to 80s-era Steve Winwood. Such diversity is reflected in multi-faceted gems like (God Created) Lock And Key, Only A Fool and Thats Rap.The seed of the project is rooted in the irresistible Chew Nails. Its a straightforward glam-rock tune, says Petralli. My take on the New York Groove, which is itself a take on the Bo Diddley beat. It has a big ol guitar riff and a singalong chorus. Its familiar territory for me, yet the vocal is perhaps more forward than most things Ive done for the band. Its the song that made me feel like I was definitely making a White Denim album.The duality of 13 is immediately apparent. The pungent funk-blues of opener (God Created) Lock And Key begins with a piece of waggish self-mythology On the thirteenth day God created White Denim but soon goes somewhere darker. This is a Beefheart / Sun Ra sort of thing, Petralli explains. I hope that its a somewhat terrifying, startling, and visceral piece for everyone that hears it. Everything I say in that song is the truth. Its about power, generational cycles of abuse, shame, violence, and survival. The things that we all understand and know and see and push down to get through the day.

title: Vape! The Grease Parody
description: Vape! The Grease Parody is a hilariously unhinged spoof of the iconic and timeless musical film Grease. The show pokes loving fun at all of the wonderful moments, sexual innuendos, outrageous characters, rivalries and secret romances from the original. The hair products may have changed, but the drama, the rivalries, and the thirst for hallway clout remain timeless. It is the musical you know and love, but dragged through a cloud of strawberry scented vapor and a TikTok filter. It's the show that you want (Ooh! Ooh! Ooh, honey!) Don't miss the Chicago premiere of this hit musical, straight from NYC. GREASE is no longer the word. Now the word is VAPE! - New York Post A must-see! A fun, irreverent night out. I couldn't stop laughing. - Hollywood Press Corps VAPE! is the one that you want! Clever, goofy and camp. - Theater Pizzazz Brash, fast and unapologetically smart. - Theaterscene.net VAPE! The Grease Parody is 85 minutes with no intermission.

title: Vape! The Grease Parody
description: Vape! The Grease Parody is a hilariously unhinged spoof of the iconic and timeless musical film Grease. The show pokes loving fun at all of the wonderful moments, sexual innuendos, outrageous characters, rivalries and secret romances from the original. The hair products may have changed, but the drama, the rivalries, and the thirst for hallway clout remain timeless. It is the musical you know and love, but dragged through a cloud of strawberry scented vapor and a TikTok filter. It's the show that you want (Ooh! Ooh! Ooh, honey!) Don't miss the Chicago premiere of this hit musical, straight from NYC. GREASE is no longer the word. Now the word is VAPE! - New York Post A must-see! A fun, irreverent night out. I couldn't stop laughing. - Hollywood Press Corps VAPE! is the one that you want! Clever, goofy and camp. - Theater Pizzazz Brash, fast and unapologetically smart. - Theaterscene.net VAPE! title: Coffee and Conversations
address: 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92102
description: Join co-editors Océane Boulais and Theodora Mautz for a conversation about the community-led zine in situ, born at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. Discover how graduate students, postdocs, and staff transform scientific experiences—from coral reef surveys and whale encounters to ice cores and lab life—into visual art, photography, poetry, and multimedia storytelling for the zine. Proceeds from the zine and community support go toward printing costs, art supplies, and events that keep collective creative action alive at Scripps, making in situ as much a grassroots organizing effort as a publication. Océane and Theodora will share the evolution of in situ , from its inaugural Seas of Change issue to its current Countercurrents volume, and explore how creative expression can complement scientific inquiry, build community across disciplines, and offer new ways of understanding our oceans. Stay for the end of the presentation, where a surprise instrument invites you to play the ocean’s frequencies yourself! The talk will take place at Mingei International Museum. Theodora Mautz is a PhD candidate in the Marine Biology program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. She currently researches cephalopod reproduction. Océane Boulais is a PhD candidate in the Applied Ocean Science program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. As an ecoacoustician, Océane listens to the ocean as a language of texture, color, and rhythm and then employs instruments to broadcast sound from healthy coral reefs into restoration reef sites, drawing coral and fish larvae home by sound via “acoustic enrichment”.

title: Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation
address: 1875 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Volcanoes have helped create our world. The continents, the air we breathe and even life itself have their origins in fire. These processes have created extraordinary ecosystems and wildlife habitats. The story of volcanoes is the story of the planet’s creation and the story of us. Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation , lets you witness the 2018 Kilauea eruption in Hawaii; see the archaeological remains of Pompeii, devastated almost 2,000 years ago by Mount Vesuvius; visit Mount Fuji in Japan, made up of three volcanoes—Fuji on top and two others hidden beneath; and marvel at the black molten lava of Ol Doinyo Lengai in Tanzania.

title: Paint and Sip: Alebrijes
address: 1649 El Prado, Suite #3, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month and Día de los Muertos with a festive evening of art, drinks, and local history! Join the San Diego History Center at Mujeres Brew House, San Diego’s first Latina-owned brewery, for a fun Paint & Sip experience. Enjoy a guided painting session led by local artist Maira Meza (@artehastalamuerte6), sip on your favorite drinks, and learn fascinating bits of local history from SDHC staff along the way. This month, we’re celebrating Día de los Muertos by painting alebrijes—colorful, creatures rooted in Mexican folk art. As you create your own alebrije, learn about their cultural significance and how they have become associated with Día de los Muertos celebrations. No painting experience needed! Whether you’re an experienced artist or picking up a paintbrush for the first time, this evening is all about having fun and getting creative. All painting materials provided Tickets: $30 — San Diego History Center Members $40 — General Admission

title: The Heavy Rotation Session 19 - Currents by Tame Impala
description: The Heavy Rotation is proud to be back at Three Top Lounge for their next session this time covering and listening to Currents by Tame Impala. If you are just hearing about The Heavy Rotation this is an idea between friends, Kalium Ewing and Grant Frahm, who were constantly sharing albums over text and wanted to connect through music in a more intentional way. They missed the feeling of hearing music in the same room and talking about it face to face. The club became their way of carving out time to slow down, listen together, and explore how music can hit differently within a community of strangers who become friends. This will be The Heavy Rotations 19th Session where they will be diving into the production and lyrics surrounding this specific album. Whether you've played this album hundreds of times, haven't listened to it in years, or will be hearing it front to back for the first time, all perspectives are welcome. Come ready to listen, question, challenge, and have an open and interesting conversation.

title: Laura Veirs w. Karl Blau
description: Laura Veirs returns with Temple Songs, her first album in four yearsand the first she has written, recorded, arranged, produced, and performed entirely on her own. I didnt know if I would write songs again, says Veirs, who spent the intervening years building a backyard studio, getting married, blending a family with four teenagers, deepening her visual art practice (painting), and expanding her music teaching. Turns out that period was a gathering phase. When I made the commitment to recording the album myself, the muse caught me again and it came together very quickly.Written and recorded in three months in the fall of 2025 in Veirs backyard Temple of Bloom studio, Temple Songs marks a new level of artistic independence. While 2022s Found Light (co-produced by Veirs and Shahzad Ismaily) was a declaration of autonomy, Temple Songs goes further: every creative decisionwhat to record, how to record it, and how it should soundwas Veirs alone. Made with just two mics and a laptop in a 10 x 14 room, the album feels unmistakably Veirs-ian, yet strikingly new.Veirs embraced the Japanese concept of wabi-sabi throughout the process, choosing not to pitch-correct vocals or edit out rough edges. I wanted to make something that sounds as organic and human as possible, she says. Mixing by Philip Weinrobe (Adrienne Lenker) adds sympathetic finishing touches to Veirs 14th solo album.Because the Temple of Bloom wasnt built for recording, the studio itself became a collaborator. Veirs paused takes for rain on the skylightor let it stay. She waited out neighbors conversations, raced to finish a sensitive vocal before a stump grinder roared to life, and included the presence of resident bluejays, passing crows, and other neighborhood sounds. These ambient intrusions lend the album an intimate, lived-in authenticity.Influences range from Mac DeMarcos commitment to trusting his personal taste to the anarchists and feminists of the late 1800s and their rallying cry, no gods, no masters. It was hard to get the white man off my shoulder, Veirs says. I wrestled with a lot of doubt. But there were many happy accidents and eventually I found a flowseeing the studio again, for the first time since my 20s, as a private place for exploration.Clocking in at a concise 30 minutes, Temple Songs 11 tracks capture a songwriter in peak form. The album is intimate, dreamy, brave and quietly defiant, built around Veirs intricate fingerstyle nylon-string guitar, vulnerable vocals, and bold electric guitar embellishments. Arc Still Bends reflects feelings of contemporary futility, offset by a hopeful chorus. Rivers Song, an ode to one of Veirs children, showcases her gift for simplicity and emotional precision. Pulse veers into art-experimental territory, culminating in a cacophonous duet between electric guitar and sax. No Masters is a sparse, punk rock call for collective self-determination, while Sunlight and Doom incorporates elemental fragments from the ancient Greek lyricist Sappho.

It's been a long year already." title: Vape! The Grease Parody
description: Vape! The Grease Parody is a hilariously unhinged spoof of the iconic and timeless musical film Grease. title: Blake Whiten - Something To Say Tour
description: Wielding a broken-glass vocal on self-penned songs that cut straight to the bone, Enchntmnt / Warner Records singer-songwriter Blake Whiten is a 21-year-old instinctive songsmith raised in Six Mile, South Carolina, whose talent launched him from bedroom videos to the biggest stages in the world. Revealed as a generational diamond in the rough, raw emotion and heavy-hearted lyrics have earned Whiten over 150 million global streams in two years since his first public performance, with more to come. Growing up on everything from Keith Whitley to Nickelback, Whiten learned guitar at seven and was penning angsty tunes by 15. After discovering the depths of his raspy vocal, a cover of Morgan Wallens Im the Problem racked up 9 million views and sent him down a new path. His solo-written 2024 single Rollin Stone amassed over 120 million streams and his co-write on Bailey Zimmermans Holding On broke the Top 40 on Billboards Hot Country Songs chart. The self-penned 2025 EP debut Six Mile captured his essence, while SiriusXM, Spotify, Apple Music, Pandora, Country Now, Holler and All Country News have lined up in support. After headlining his Rollin Stone Tour and making his Grand Ole Opry debut in early 2026, Whitens first album Something to Say, features 12 co-written songs, as his confessional instincts collide with pitch-black alt-rock intensity. Currently on Bailey Zimmermans Different Night Same Rodeo Tour, hell take the stage in stadiums this summer for Wallens Still the Problem Tour 2026.Story Behind The Song Acoustic Experience includes:One Event TicketExclusive Access to the Fan Voted Story Behind The Song Acoustic ExperienceOne VIP-Exclusive Poster Signed by Blake WhitenOne Commemorative VIP LaminateEarly Entry (Where Applicable)Early Access Merchandise Shopping (Where Applicable)This package does NOT include a meet & greet with Blake Whiten.

title: Meteorites as Artistic Matter
address: 1450 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Speakers: Ulrike Arnold , Artist; Gerard van Belle, PhD , Former Director of Science at Lowell Observatory; and Rachel Jans, PhD , Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at The San Diego Museum of Art MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater Meteorites as Artistic Matter brings together internationally acclaimed artist Ulrike Arnold, astronomer Gerard van Belle, and the Museum’s Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art Rachel Jans, PhD, for a fascinating interdisciplinary conversation exploring the intersection of art, science, and the cosmos. Known for incorporating meteorite dust and pigments gathered from some of the world’s most remote landscapes into her paintings, Arnold will discuss how celestial and earthly materials become powerful artistic media. Joined by van Belle’s astronomical perspective and Jans’s expertise on the work of Sigmar Polke, a German artist also known for incorporating unconventional materials into his work, and contemporary artistic practice, this engaging guest lecture offers a rare opportunity to discover how meteorites inspire creativity, expand our understanding of materiality, and connect artistic expression with the vast universe beyond our planet. Following the lecture, guests are invited to enjoy a guided tour led by our docent team. Please note, this lecture is in-person only and held at the MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater in Balboa Park. $15 members and students | $20 seniors and military | $30 nonmembers This lecture is presented as a part of the Guest Lecture Series , which offers a platform for renowned scholars and experts from the art world to share their insights and knowledge on topics related to art history, art theory, and the museum’s collections.

title: Nat at Night
venue: San Diego Natural History Museum (The Nat)
address: 1788 El Prado, Balboa Park, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: On select Fridays, the San Diego Natural History Museum is open late just for you. Enjoy access to all open exhibitions and our rooftop deck for good views and great vibes. The rooftop is open to all visitors and serves beer, wine, non-alcoholic drinks , and food from Wolf in the Woods. Take a selfie with a megalodon shark, see scientists at work in our Paleo Center , admire glittering gems, get a close up look at spiders and snakes, and so much more. Best of all, get a look at our brand-new exhibition, Washed Ashore: Art to Save the Sea and grab a drink in the dive bar while chatting with a scientist. On select dates, channel your inner artist with Sketchparty , get competitive during trivia, or unwind while listening to the rooftop DJ. Hungry for more? The Craft Taco , located inside the Atrium, is a vibrant taco restaurant offering a delectable fusion of flavors and artisanal creations. They offer made-to-order tacos featuring signature blue corn tortillas, delectable burritos and bowls, and a variety of drinks and coffees. Admission is half-price after 5 PM, and parking is free after 6 PM. You can buy your tickets online in advance or buy them at the door the night of . As always, members of The Nat and Explorer pass holders enjoy free general admission.

title: Sacred Movement, Painted Prayers
address: 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92102
description: Experience the intersection of living craft, tradition, and movement. Begin the evening with a performance of Nihon Buyo —Japanese classical dance—by acclaimed dancer Ichinosuke Umekawa. Formally trained in ballet and Kabuki theater, Umekawa brings folk narratives to life through fluid grace and masterful expression. Following the performance, join Guest Curator Meher McArthur to enjoy an advance preview of Painted Prayers — The Japanese Folk Art Tradition of Ema before the exhibition opens to the public the next day. McArthur will share her research and insights into these hand-painted wooden prayer tablets, illuminating the rich connections between sacred visual art, human devotion, and performing craft.

title: Candlelight Concert
address: 1875 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Candlelight Concerts are a series of original music concerts created by Fever aimed at democratizing access to culture by allowing people all over the world to enjoy live music candlelit performances played by local musicians in various stunning locations illuminated by thousands of candles. Candlelight was initially conceived as a classical music series with concerts featuring works from the greatest composers, such as Vivaldi, Mozart, and Chopin. Now, the ever-growing list of programs includes a wide variety of themes and genres, including tributes to contemporary like Queen, ABBA, Coldplay, and Ed Sheeran, as well as shows dedicated to K-Pop, movie soundtracks and many more. This multi-sensory experience has also evolved to feature different elements, such as ballet dancers or aerial performers, as well as other genres, such as jazz, soul, opera, flamenco, and more. Candlelight Concerts are present in more than 100 cities worldwide, with over 3 Million guests in attendance to date

description: Early access to galleries at 9 a.m. On the third Saturday of every month, we open our doors one hour before the museum opens to the public and screen a documentary with house lights on and the soundtrack volume low. And if you want to stay and enjoy the museum all day? You can! Accessibility Morning features a special film screening of a documentary at 10 a.m. with house lights on and the soundtrack volume low. title: Hawktober at Lake Morena
venue: Lake Morena County Park,2550 Lake Morena Dr, Campo, CA 91906, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

title: A Space for All of Us
address: 1350 El Prado, Balboa Park, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Sensory-Friendly Quiet Mornings at the Museum The Museum’s sensory-friendly quiet hours are held every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. This time is dedicated to creating a calmer, quieter museum experience. We remain open to the public during this time, and all are welcome to visit the Museum. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. Noise-blocking headphones are free for check-out at the main Admissions desk and the entrance to the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibition, Exhibit features in the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibit will remain on, and all exhibits will be fully turned on at 11 a.m. Admission purchased during sensory-friendly quiet hours is the same as standard admission and applies to the entire day. Please contact publicprograms@museumofus.org with any questions.

title: Compositions: An Evening Of Katie Jenkins
description: Pointeworks presents COMPOSITIONS: An Evening of Katie Jenkins, a celebration of Resident Composer Katie Jenkins featuring three original ballet commissions performed with live music. Curated by Artistic Director Sophie Williams, the evening brings together an international cast of world-class artists for a program dedicated entirely to female voices in both choreography and composition. The program features the return of Laine Habony's Chasing Shadows, a striking piano solo work, alongside Jacquelyn Long's Moving Forces for six dancers, piano, and violin. The evening culminates in a world premiere by acclaimed choreographer Hélène Simoneau, featuring a soaring new score for live string quartet.

title: Hawktober at Waterfront Park
venue: Waterfront Park,1600 Pacific Hwy, San Diego, CA 92101, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

title: Vienna Royal Orchestra: Viva Mozart 270
description: VIENNA ROYAL ORCHESTRA:VIVA MOZART 270 Matthew Busse, Conductor Tian Jiang,Piano Shay Mowbray, piano Anson Wong, piano From Carnegie Hall to Jacobs Music Center... Following its New York performance this summer at Carnegie Hall, the Vienna Royal Orchestra brings its VIVA MOZART 270 celebration to Jacobs Music Center in San Diego. This special concert honors the 270th anniversary of the birth of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, one of history's most beloved and influential musical geniuses. Audiences will enjoy an inspiring program of Mozart's timeless masterpieces, performed by distinguished musicians from Europe and the United States. Internationally celebrated pianist Tian Jiang appears as soloist in Mozart's Piano Concerto No. 23 in A Major, K. 488. Praised as "a thoughtful interpreter" by The New York Times and "a deeply persuasive Mozartean" by The Los Angeles Times, he is recognized for performances that combine poetic artistry, technical mastery, and expressive depth.

title: Wellness Wednesdays (Virtual) - SD Nights
description: Join our VIRTUAL Wellness Wednesday Yoga Class! Each session features a mindful and rejuvenating yoga practice designed specifically for teens to build strength, flexibility, balance, and focus. Led by an experienced yoga instructor, the class provides expert guidance in a positive and supportive environment while encouraging mindfulness, self-confidence, and overall well-being. Participants will leave each session feeling refreshed, accomplished, and empowered in both body and mind.  SD Nights - short for San Diego/Safe Destination Nights - is a FREE program developed by the County of San Diego Department of Parks and Recreation designed to provide teens, ages 10 to 18, with safe places to recreate after school and during critical hours.  For more information and to register, call 619-541-5188 or email: juancarlos.robles@sdcounty.ca.gov mailto:juancarlos.robles@sdcounty.ca.gov

title: Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation
address: 1875 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Volcanoes have helped create our world. The continents, the air we breathe and even life itself have their origins in fire. These processes have created extraordinary ecosystems and wildlife habitats. The story of volcanoes is the story of the planet’s creation and the story of us. Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation , lets you witness the 2018 Kilauea eruption in Hawaii; see the archaeological remains of Pompeii, devastated almost 2,000 years ago by Mount Vesuvius; visit Mount Fuji in Japan, made up of three volcanoes—Fuji on top and two others hidden beneath; and marvel at the black molten lava of Ol Doinyo Lengai in Tanzania.

description: The world-famous Willy Wonka is opening the gates to his mysterious factory, but only to a lucky few. Based on the famous novel by Roald Dahl, Charlie and the Chocolate Factory features an original score composed by Marc Shaiman and contains songs from the motion picture including “The Candy Man,” “I’ve Got a Golden Ticket,” “Oompa Loompa Song,” and “Pure Imagination.” Pajama Night is Friday, October 30 at 7pm. Come in your favorite PJs (Halloween costumes count!) and get a special gift! PLUS! Will you be the lucky patron who finds the golden ticket at your performance? Get your tickets to the show and find out! ASL-Interpreted performance on Saturday, November 7 at 2pm. All ages are welcome! Anticipated running time: 2 hours, 30 minutes, including intermission. title: Painted Prayers: Japanese Ema Votive Plaques
address: 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92102
description: Ema (literally, “picture horse”) are wooden votive plaques on which visitors to Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples have for centuries written their prayers and wishes for the _kami _or Buddhist deities to read. Though these plaques originally featured horses, they evolved to feature many different images associated with various wishes, from good fortune to health to love and relationships. In conjunction with the exhibition Painted Prayers: The Japanese Folk Art Tradition of Ema , exhibition curator and Japanese art historian, Meher McArthur will explore the history of these votive plaques, the meanings behind some of the images, and their role in contemporary Japanese spiritual culture.

title: Hawktober at Lamar County Park
venue: Lamar County Park,3180 Bancroft Dr, Spring Valley, CA 91977, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

title: San Diego Opera Presents: RIGOLETTO
description: Making jokes is what Rigoletto does for a living, serving as court jester to the predatory Duke of Mantua. But the joke may be on him when one of his jests enrages Count Monterone, the father of the Duke's latest victim, unleashing a curse with dangerous consequences for Rigoletto and his beautiful daughter Gilda. Packed with spectacular arias like "La donna e mobile," "Caro nome," and the stunning quartet "Bella figlia dell'amore," Verdi's sublime tale of betrayal, sacrifice, and revenge will hold you spellbound from start to finish.

title: Koto Lessons
address: 2215 Pan American Road East, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Koto, also called kin, long Japanese board zither having 13 silk strings and movable bridges. The body of the instrument is made of paulownia wood and is about 190 cm (74 inches) long. When the performer is kneeling or seated on the floor, the koto is held off the floor by two legs or a bridge-storage box; in most modern concerts, the instrument is placed on a stand so the performer can sit on a chair. The koto is played by plucking the strings with the thumb and first two fingers of the right hand, which are fitted with ivory plectrums called tsume. The left hand, in traditions after the 16th century, may alter the pitch or sound of each string by pressing or manipulating the strings to the left of the bridges. Various pentatonic tunings are used, depending on the type of music being played. The koto appeared in the Japanese court during the 8th century and was called the gakusō. Schools for the bourgeois were established in the 16th century. Two of these—Ikuta (started in the 17th century) and Yamada (opened in the 18th century)—continue to the present day. Solo (danmono) and chamber (sankyoku) music dominate the repertory, and in the latter form the koto player often sings as well. title: Art in the Evening: The Moods of Early Russian Art
description: Join us for a special Art in the Evening program featuring Justin Willson, Curator at The Icon Museum and Study Center in Clinton, Massachusetts, as he illuminates one of the most transformative periods in Russian icon painting. Drawing upon exceptional works in the Timken collection, Willson will trace developments in style and patronage across fifteenth- and sixteenth-century Muscovy, beginning with painters in the circle of Dionisiy and revealing how a sweeping religious revival reshaped the artistic and spiritual character of early Russian art. Set against the intimate backdrop of the Museum’s galleries, the evening offers a rare opportunity to experience the Timken’s distinguished collection of Russian icons through the perspective of a leading scholar in the field. Guests are invited to enjoy wine and curated nibbles before the lecture, followed by an engaging conversation that brings new insight to works whose beauty and spiritual resonance have endured for centuries. The lecture coincides with the release of Wilson’s book, The Moods of Early Russian Art (University of Chicago Press, 2026). Copies of the book will be available for purchase at the event.

description: Join award-winning Chef Spencer Hunter of Lia’s Lumpia on October 25, 2026, from 6:00–8:00 PM at the San Diego History Center for a Kamayan feast celebrating Filipino American History Month. A San Diego native and finalist on Food Network’s Great Food Truck Race, Chef Spencer honors his Filipino grandmother’s culinary legacy while blending it with his African American roots. He has taken first place for his Sisig Lumpia, cheffed for distinguished clientele ranging from corporate leaders to members of the British Royal Family, and continues to redefine what modern fusion cuisine can be. Kamayan is a traditional Filipino style of communal dining where food is spread across a table lined with fresh banana leaves and shared by everyone. SDHC’s Kamayan feast will feature: Appetizers: Bacon Jalapeño Popper Lumpia Filipino Cheese and Charcuterie Grazing Table Feast: Mango Mixed Greens Salad (plated at each seat) Sinigang Pork Bone Broth (plated at each seat) JUMBO Lola’s Pork LUMPIA Calamansi Chicken Wings Classic Chicken Adobo Bangus (Milkfish) Sisig Braised Beef & Potatoes Bistec Steamed Jasmine Rice Vegetable Pancit Noodles Pickled Cucumbers & Cherry Tomatoes Sweet Chili Sauce, Garlic Vinegar, Sriracha, Soy Sauce Freshly sliced fruit Sweet Bites: Guava Cream Cheese LUMPIA Tickets include appetizers, kamayan feast, complimentary beverages, and after-hours admission to SDHC exhibits, including Taste San Diego: Filipino Culinary Journeys. title: Art + Design Workshop: Floral Arranging
description: Celebrate the beauty and abundance of the season with a morning of floral design at the Timken. Inspired by the rich colors, textures, and graceful compositions found in the Museum’s collection, this hands-on workshop invites participants to create an elegant autumn arrangement using a thoughtfully selected palette of seasonal flowers and foliage. Under the guidance of a professional floral designer, participants will explore the principles of balance, color, form, and movement that unite the traditions of painting and floral design. Each guest will create a distinctive arrangement to take home. No prior floral design experience is necessary. Workshop fee includes all materials, tools, and light refreshments. About the Artist: Anne Latham is a floral designer, photographer, ceramicist, garden designer, and artist. As the principal designer of Three Swords Floral Co., she leads an exceptional team of designers, traveling around California and Hawai’i to craft floral experiences for private estates, destination weddings, and discreet brand activations. Anne has been flowering since 2015, following her formal training as a bookbinder and lithographer at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Her Midwestern roots and background as an artist, studio assistant, and time spent in the hospitality industry continue to inform her refined, grounded, and deeply personal approach to floral design.

title: Dr. Jekyll & Mr. Hyde (1920) Played by David Marsh
description: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde (1920) Witness one of silent cinema's most chilling performances in Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde! John Barrymore delivers a mesmerizing transformation in this dark tale of science gone horribly wrong, as a brilliant doctor unleashes his sinister alter ego with shocking consequences that spiral beyond his control. Join us for this gripping and gothic masterpiece featuring live organ accompaniment tailored to the film by David Marsh. Arrive early and stay late for fun and informative activities! This screening is part of our Silent Movie Mondays series at the Balboa Theatre. Join us at this historic venue and step back a century, when audiences cheered, the organ came alive, and silent films glowed on the big screen. Learn more at sandiegotheatres.org.

title: Wellness Wednesdays (Virtual) - SD Nights
description: Join our VIRTUAL Wellness Wednesday Yoga Class! Each session features a mindful and rejuvenating yoga practice designed specifically for teens to build strength, flexibility, balance, and focus. Led by an experienced yoga instructor, the class provides expert guidance in a positive and supportive environment while encouraging mindfulness, self-confidence, and overall well-being. Participants will leave each session feeling refreshed, accomplished, and empowered in both body and mind.  SD Nights - short for San Diego/Safe Destination Nights - is a FREE program developed by the County of San Diego Department of Parks and Recreation designed to provide teens, ages 10 to 18, with safe places to recreate after school and during critical hours.  For more information and to register, call 619-541-5188 or email: juancarlos.robles@sdcounty.ca.gov mailto:juancarlos.robles@sdcounty.ca.gov

title: Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation
address: 1875 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Volcanoes have helped create our world. The continents, the air we breathe and even life itself have their origins in fire. These processes have created extraordinary ecosystems and wildlife habitats. The story of volcanoes is the story of the planet’s creation and the story of us. Volcanoes: The Fires of Creation , lets you witness the 2018 Kilauea eruption in Hawaii; see the archaeological remains of Pompeii, devastated almost 2,000 years ago by Mount Vesuvius; visit Mount Fuji in Japan, made up of three volcanoes—Fuji on top and two others hidden beneath; and marvel at the black molten lava of Ol Doinyo Lengai in Tanzania.

title: Artistic Practice: Roxana Velázquez in Conversation with Artist Betsabeé Romero
address: 1450 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Speakers: Roxana Velázquez , Maruja Baldwin Executive Director and CEO at The San Diego Museum of Art, and Betsabeé Romero , Artist MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater Presented in conjunction with the Museum’s Día de los Muertos celebration , this special conversation introduces internationally acclaimed Mexican artist Betsabeé Romero. In dialogue with SDMA Executive Director and CEO Roxana Velázquez, Romero will discuss her artistic practice, the themes of memory, migration, identity, and cultural heritage that define her work, and the inspiration behind her site-specific project for the Museum. This conversation offers audiences an opportunity to meet the artist behind one of the season’s most anticipated installations and to discover how contemporary art can bridge tradition and innovation. Following the lecture, guests are invited to enjoy a guided tour led by our docent team. Please note, this lecture is in-person only and held at the MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater in Balboa Park. $15 members and students | $20 seniors and military | $30 nonmembers This lecture is presented as a part of the Guest Lecture Series , which offers a platform for renowned scholars and experts from the art world to share their insights and knowledge on topics related to art history, art theory, and the museum’s collections. Sponsored by The San Diego Museum of Art Docent Council .

title: Hawktober at El Monte County Park
venue: El Monte County Park,15805 El Monte Rd, Lakeside, CA 92040, USA
description: Hawktober is our annual celebration of local birds of prey, including hawks, owls, and falcons. This marks the event's eighth year offering FREE workshops at parks, campgrounds and wilderness preserves across San Diego County.  Events are free and open to all ages, starting October 3. Explore multiple workshops to meet different birds and rangers.  What to Expect:    * Live raptors: Meet ambassador birds like hawks, owls, and falcons up close and learn about their unique behaviors and adaptations.   * Fun facts: Discover how these birds live, what they eat, how they hunt, when they're active, and special traits like speed, camouflage, or night vision.   * Bird tales: Each event features different birds—each with a name and story—shared by passionate rangers.   * Special perk: Grab limited-edition Hawktober trading cards (while supplies last), complete with stats like wingspan, weight, and fun facts.  For more information, visit sdparks.org/hawktober https://www.sdparks.org/hawktober/ .

title: More Than Pink Walk
address: San Diego, CA
description: The MORE THAN PINK Walk, Susan G. Komen’s largest fundraising event series, evolved from the Race for the Cure in 2018. Each year, we host over 100,000 participants at our 40+ in-person (and one virtual) walks across the U.S. Since the first Walk in 2018, our participants have raised more than $60 million dollars and continue to be a part of a community committed to our vision of a world without breast cancer. With inclusive and accessible options for people of all ages and abilities – including breast cancer survivors, those currently in treatment for breast cancer and people living with metastatic breast cancer – the Walk provides participants the opportunity to come together and connect in meaningful ways. It allows us to focus on sharing our passion, sharing our stories and connecting with others, all while fundraising to support life-saving programs and research. Our finish line is a world without breast cancer, and we know the only way we can get there is together.

title: A Space for All of Us

description: Sensory-Friendly Quiet Mornings at the Museum The Museum’s sensory-friendly quiet hours are held every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. This time is dedicated to creating a calmer, quieter museum experience. We remain open to the public during this time, and all are welcome to visit the Museum. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. Noise-blocking headphones are free for check-out at the main Admissions desk and the entrance to the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibition, Exhibit features in the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibit will remain on, and all exhibits will be fully turned on at 11 a.m. Admission purchased during sensory-friendly quiet hours is the same as standard admission and applies to the entire day. Please contact publicprograms@museumofus.org with any questions.

title: Día de los Muertos at SDMA
address: 1450 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Come together with family, friends, and the community at large at a special, free community event celebrating and honoring Día de los Muertos. Enjoy live performances, family-friendly art-making activities, and a special Día de los Muertos ofrenda created by visiting artist Betsabeé Romero in collaboration with local San Diego students, all in the Balboa Park Plaza de Panama in front of The San Diego Museum of Art and free to the community. Through artist-designed artmaking activities, community members will be invited to honor loved ones, share memories, and contribute meaningful objects and creative responses to the ofrenda on view in the plaza. Romero will join the Museum community for the inauguration of the SDMA ofrenda on Sunday, November 1 at 11:00 a.m. on the Museum’s front steps. The Taco Party , a gathering featuring unlimited street-style tacos, refreshing beverages, music, and a festive atmosphere, is a ticketed event complementing Día de los Muertos at SDMA. Free admission to The San Diego Museum of Art (SDMA) and the Museum of Photographic Arts at The San Diego Museum of Art (MOPA@SDMA) on Sunday, November 1 at noon–5:00 p.m. further complements the Día de los Muertos celebration.

title: The Taco Party
address: 1450 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Join us for The Taco Party, a lively gathering featuring unlimited street-style tacos, refreshing beverages, music, and a festive atmosphere, all in the Museum’s sculpture court and garden. Designed as a fun and welcoming celebration for all ages, The Taco Party brings together great food, community, and the joyful spirit of Día de los Muertos. The Taco Party is part of Día de los Muertos at SDMA , a day of community highlighting a special ofrenda created by the community and designed by this season’s Visiting Artist Betsabeé Romero, transforming the Museum into a powerful tribute to remembrance and celebration. The Taco Party is a special ticketed portion of the Día de los Muertos celebration bringing together great food, community, and the joyful spirit of the holiday. The Taco Party is designed as a fun and welcoming celebration for all ages. Event includes: Unlimited taco tastings from stations hosted by participating local restaurants and taco vendors One complimentary Panama 66 margarita, beer on tap from Mujeres Brew House , or agua fresca included with ticket purchase; Additional beverages available for purchase through Panama 66 bar Cold brew, coffee, matcha, and more from Marta Refreshing De La Calle Tepache , a modern take on the traditional Mexican fermented pineapple beverage Themed photo booth Live music by San Diego-based Latin jazz group Quinteto Caballero Interactive art-making activities led by Museum educators And more to be announced… The Taco Party also continues the year-long centennial celebration marking the 100th year of The San Diego Museum of Art serving the community through art and bringing the world’s greatest art to the region. Both museums will be free and open to the public on this day: SDMA: noon–5:00 p.m. MOPA@SDMA: 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Don’t miss art by Visiting Artist Betsabeé Romero as part of the Día de los Muertos at SDMA community ofrenda in front of The San Diego Museum of Art and in Betsabeé Romero: Tejiendo Redes at MOPA@SDMA. Plus, explore art from Mexican greats including Diego Rivera, Manuel Álvarez Bravo, Rufino Tamayo, and more, as well as artists from around the world, at The San Diego Museum of Art. Tickets to The Taco Party are now on sale! Tickets: $50 Members | $60 Nonmembers | $20 Youth (ages 0-6)

title: Tusk: The Classic Fleetwood Mac Tribute
description: Playing the hits and deep cuts spanning the career of Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame group Fleetwood Mac, Tusk has been crisscrossing the country since 2008 as The Classic Fleetwood Mac Tribute. Five pro musicians turned into masters of their trade through decades of individual music study, live performance, creative risk and devotion to the art. TUSK features note-perfect renditions of both the solo and full band songs, with each member specializing in one of the core lineup of Fleetwood Mac (Lindsey Buckingham, Stevie Nicks, Christine McVie, John McVie, and Mick Fleetwood). They possess an electric stage presence that can only come from well over a decade touring together. Truly the best at what they do, TUSK is unmatched in their tribute to one of the greatest bands of all time.

title: The Outsiders (Touring)
description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

title: JÉRÉMY CHARBONNEL
address: 8878 Clairemont Mesa Blvd, San Diego, CA 92123
description: Mais où est-ce que ça a merdé ? Jérémy Charbonnel livre ses galères de papa célibataire qui se bat pour ne pas finir comme son père… mais pas que! Dans ce spectacle authentique et sincère, Jérémy est en quête de réponses pour mieux comprendre sa vie. Mais pour trouver des réponses, encore faut-il se poser les bonnes questions... Avec un humour caustique et une touche de tendresse, il transforme ses échecs en leçons de vie, nous montrant qu'il faut parfois tout perdre pour mieux se retrouver. Un spectacle drôle, touchant, et surprenant! L'accès au Mic Drop est réservé aux personnes âgées de 21

title: The Outsiders (Touring)
description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

title: Spinning Resistance: Women, Cloth, and the Long Memory of 1776
address: 1649 El Prado, Suite #3, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: The spinning wheel keeps showing up at moments of political crisis — and it’s never just about spinning. In the 1760s, American women turned spinning bees into public acts of resistance against British taxation. Arts and Crafts reformers claimed it as a rebuke to industrial capitalism. In the 1920s, Gandhi made the charkha the emblem of Indian independence from the British Empire. Twentieth-century American women, meanwhile, rediscovered it as a symbol of a revolutionary female tradition the original 1776 had denied them — decorating their homes with it, wearing the loose clothing it evoked, claiming the Daughters of Liberty as their own foremothers. But the spinning wheel casts a longer shadow: enslaved women spun and wove too, and the cotton that fed industrial production had been harvested by coerced labor for generations. Join the San Diego History Center for another program in our America at 250 series as historian Molly McClain explores the history of the spinning wheel across three continents and 150 years to ask what commemorative culture commemorates — and who gets to decide. Molly McClain (PhD, Yale) is a professor of history at the University of San Diego. Her research focuses on women’s history, philanthropy, and cultural history more broadly. A ninth-generation San Diegan, she is the author of four books and numerous articles, including Ellen Browning Scripps: New Money and American Philanthropy (2017). McClain’s public history work includes over a decade as editor of The Journal of San Diego History and the successful designation of the La Jolla Park Coastal Historic District to the National Register of Historic Places in 2024. General tickets: $20 Museum Members: $10

description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

title: Felt Together
address: 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA, 92102
description: Inspired by the intricate bas-relief needlework and cozy scenes featured in My Bed: Enchanting Ways to Fall Asleep Around the World , our newest Together workshop series, Felt Together , explores the art of needle felting. The series is led by Sophie Ancel, a fiber artist who blends rich textures and thoughtful layering to bring imaginative landscapes to life. Through her process-driven approach to wool and textile art, she brings a warm, accessible perspective to the world of living craft. Friday, November 6, 2026 | 5-7pm In November, create a night sky scene out of wool. Sophie will teach you how to layer and mix colorful fibers to build a cozy scene with glowing windows, trees, and stars. The Together series at Mingei invites makers of all skill levels to come together and create in a supportive, low-pressure environment. Past iterations— Sew Together, Weave Together , Dye Together , Stitch Together , Clay Together, and Knot Together —explore a variety of craft techniques while emphasizing collaboration, experimentation, and hands-on learning. Each workshop encourages participants to connect with materials, try new skills, and enjoy the process of making together.

title: The Outsiders (Touring)
description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

description: Sensory-Friendly Quiet Mornings at the Museum The Museum’s sensory-friendly quiet hours are held every Sunday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. This time is dedicated to creating a calmer, quieter museum experience. We remain open to the public during this time, and all are welcome to visit the Museum. During this time, specific exhibit features in the main Museum building will be turned off to minimize audio and visual stimulation. Noise-blocking headphones are free for check-out at the main Admissions desk and the entrance to the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibition, Exhibit features in the Cannibals: Myth & Reality exhibit will remain on, and all exhibits will be fully turned on at 11 a.m. Admission purchased during sensory-friendly quiet hours is the same as standard admission and applies to the entire day. Please contact publicprograms@museumofus.org with any questions.

title: Michael Blaustein: The Taste Me Tour: The Final Leg
description: Michael Blaustein is one of the fastest rising stand up comedians working today. His viral stand up comedy clips have amassed over 900 Million views across all social media platforms. He has sold out venues across the world, most recently closing out his successful 2025 tour year with over 70,000 tickets sold. When he's not on the road, he's co-hosting the chart topping hit comedy podcast Stiff Socks with Trevor Wallace, which has over 70 Million downloads. Michael has also worked with brands such as Manscaped, Liquid Death, and BetterHelp. Now he returns to the stage for the final leg of his wildly successful Taste Me Tour, giving fans one last chance to catch this set live.

title: Susan G Komen 3 Day Walk
address: San Diego, CA
description: Your Susan G. Komen 3-Day ® starts the moment you make the commitment. Your 3-Day coaches will support you as you train and fundraise. Our amazing community of walkers, crew, and volunteers will welcome you into our Pink Bubble as you get ready to take an incredible journey to end breast cancer forever. You can customize your journey with a 1-Day, 2-Day or full 3-Day experience. Choose whichever commitment, distance and fundraising minimum is right for you. Every step matters. Every dollar raised helps us fulfill our mission. 1 DAY, 20 MILES Raise $750. A great way to sample the 3-Day experience, Sunday, November 15. 2 DAYS, 40 MILES Raise $1,800. Step it up for an extra challenge, Saturday and Sunday, November 14-15. 3 DAYS, 60 MILES Raise $2,300. Join us for the full 3-Day experience, Friday, Saturday and Sunday, November 13-15. When you choose the 3-Day Route , your first day begins with an inspirational Opening Ceremony where the adrenaline and anticipation of taking on 60 miles is like nothing you’ve ever experienced before. The feelings of pride and strength you’ll realize while walking 60 miles through San Diego’s cool surfside neighborhoods are only matched by the spirit and gratitude of the communities you encounter and those you are helping along the way. You’ll walk along the Pacific Coast Highway and will be wowed by the beauty of Del Mar, Torrey Pines and Mission Bay! You’ll spend Friday and Saturday night with your fellow participants in our outdoor camp at Sunset Point Park. Hotel options are available at your own expense . When you choose the 2-Day Route , your first day begins on Saturday, November 14 with an energetic welcome and walk out. You’ll walk approximately 40 miles over the course of two days, with breaks and lunch along the route. You’ll join us at the end of your first day for a moving Honor Ceremony where we honor and share stories of those we’ve lost, those still fighting and our survivors and thrivers living with metastatic breast cancer. You’ll spend Saturday night with your fellow participants in our outdoor camp at Sunset Point Park, with an option to camp on Friday night as well, if you wish. When you choose the 1-Day Route , your journey begins Sunday, November 15 where you join in with our 2-Day and 3-Day walkers for a welcome and walk out on the final day of the 3-Day journey. Or you can choose to arrive on Saturday and spend the night with us in camp. For all participants, your adventure culminates in a Finish Line Festival and Closing Ceremony celebrating all you’ve accomplished, remembering those we have lost, and honoring those who are in the fight of their lives. Whether you walk 20, 40 or 60 miles, you’ll do so in the embrace of the dedicated 3-Day community, sharing stories, eating meals together and making new friends. There’s no question that the 3-Day is a hard journey, but we all know, it’s not as hard as breast cancer. It’s not as hard as getting bad news at your latest scan. It’s not as hard as saying goodbye. We walk because we must. We walk for ourselves, our sisters, mothers, fathers, daughters, sons and friends. We walk because we can’t sit idly by watching while breast cancer still exists in the world. Since 2003, we’ve raised more than $927 million to save lives, support community programs, and make huge strides in breast cancer research and access to care. The Susan G. Komen 3-Day is an experience you’ll never forget. It’s why our walkers come back year after year to recommit their time and energy to put an end to breast cancer once and for all. Register and join us.

description: SDCAMA art shows display the living art of today; you can hold it in your hands and take it into your life. description: Come see real Astronomers from the San Diego Astronomy Association and look through their big, beautiful telescopes at Mother Nature's night light display. title: Koto Lessons
address: 2215 Pan American Road East, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: Koto, also called kin, long Japanese board zither having 13 silk strings and movable bridges. The body of the instrument is made of paulownia wood and is about 190 cm (74 inches) long. When the performer is kneeling or seated on the floor, the koto is held off the floor by two legs or a bridge-storage box; in most modern concerts, the instrument is placed on a stand so the performer can sit on a chair. The koto is played by plucking the strings with the thumb and first two fingers of the right hand, which are fitted with ivory plectrums called tsume. The left hand, in traditions after the 16th century, may alter the pitch or sound of each string by pressing or manipulating the strings to the left of the bridges. Various pentatonic tunings are used, depending on the type of music being played. The koto appeared in the Japanese court during the 8th century and was called the gakusō. Schools for the bourgeois were established in the 16th century. Two of these—Ikuta (started in the 17th century) and Yamada (opened in the 18th century)—continue to the present day. Solo (danmono) and chamber (sankyoku) music dominate the repertory, and in the latter form the koto player often sings as well. description: Fiesta Island Time Trials Fiesta Island Time Trials is San Diego's original time trial series since 1968, sponsored by San Diego Bicycle Club. Time trials are known as the race of truth, it is the cyclist against the clock. Athletes select category and distance, 3 laps (20km) or 6 laps (40km) around Fiesta Island, juniors will ride one or two laps. Single riders, tandems, and teams all compete for top honors and island records or come out and test their fitness. An awards ceremony will be held after the last athlete finishes. Top six finishers in each category will be eligible to earn points towards series competition. Awards will be given to series winners at the last race of the series.

title: Wine & Masters: Beyond Champagne
description: From the storied vineyards of Champagne to the hills of northern Italy, Catalonia, England, and California, sparkling wine takes on a distinctive character shaped by place, tradition, and technique. This lively exploration travels beyond Champagne to reveal how celebrated sparkling wines—including Prosecco, Cava, Franciacorta, Sekt, and emerging New World expressions—reflect the grapes, landscapes, and cultures from which they come. Along the way, discover what distinguishes each style and why the world’s fascination with bubbles extends far beyond France. About the Speaker: Dane Kuta is a Level 2 Certified Sommelier, Champagne Master, Bordeaux Master, Champagne MOOC, Italian Wine Professional, and Napa Valley Wine Expert. He has taught wine appreciation at San Diego State University; California State University, San Marcos; and MiraCosta College and is a member of the Guild of Sommeliers. PROGRAM 4:00 – 4:30 Wine & Hors d’Oeuvres Reception 4:30 – 5:15 Part One: Lecture with Dane Kuta 5:15 – 5:30 Dessert Intermission 5:30 – 6:30 Part Two: Sparkling Wine Tasting ‍
